name: Beat actions
summary: A beat can do more than move a figure. It can play a recording you made, change only the shader, clothes, eyes or skin, and start or stop a sound. A voice beat waits for its recording to finish.
helps: Make a figure say hello and change its shader while it waves, all on the same strip, without anything flashing.
where2d: Animate panel: Beat actions, under Beat strip.
whereVR: Capture face > Animate > Beat strip, then the voice and shader rows

d2: Record a line for a figure in Narration.
Open the Animate panel and put the clock where you want the voice to start.
Press Add voice beat. The hold is the length of the recording.
Press Add shader beat to add a change of shader at the clock.
Press Play and watch and listen. Press Stop to put everything back.
vr: Record a line for a figure in Narration.
Open the wrist menu, then Capture face, Animate, Beat strip.
Press Add voice and pick your recording. Press Add shader beat.
Press Play. Press Stop to put everything back.
use: a voice beat holds for the length of its recording, so the next beat waits
a shader beat leaves the clothes and the rest of the look alone
a clothes piece that is not cleared is left out with a message
looks change no faster than every 0.4 seconds, so nothing flashes
Stop and Pause stop the voice and any sound
a friend sees the looks and poses and does not start your voice or sounds.

changes.note: Beats can now play a recording and change just the shader, clothes or eyes, so record a line, press Add voice beat, then Add shader beat, and press Play.
